speaker: Abhinavagupta (devotee's voice, first-person colophon)
question: What does the dated, signed hymn accomplish?
premises: In the month of Pauṣa, on the dark tenth, Abhinavagupta made this hymn: dated, signed.

By whom (yena) — devotee or hymn, undivided in effect — the pervasive (vibhuḥ), compassionate (dayāluḥ) Lord becomes (bhavati), pacifies (śamayati) the world's desert-heat of becoming — instantly (jhaṭiti).
The dated hymn turns outward: private recognition cools the world.
The verse moves from colophon to pacification to speed: inward dissolution (v.1) to world-pacification.
inference: Dated and signed: the hymn turns outward, private recognition cools the world.
uncertainties: Whether 'yena' refers to devotee or hymn is unresolved.
Whether 'bhavamarusantāpa' is physical or existential heat is unresolved.
